source: fn f(n:Int)->Int {case n {0->{let a=n+1 let b=a+2 let c=b+3 c} 1->{let a=n+1 let b=a+2 let c=b+3 c} 2->{let a=n+1 let b=a+2 let c=b+3 c} 3->{let a=n+1 let b=a+2 let c=b+3 c} 4->{let a=n+1 let b=a+2 let c=b+3 c} 5->{let a=n+1 let b=a+2 let c=b+3 c} 6->{let a=n+1 let b=a+2 let c=b+3 c} 7->{let a=n+1 let b=a+2 let c=b+3 c} _->n+f(n-1)}} pub fn main()->Nil {echo f(600) Nil}
limitations: One bounded non-tail recursion workload, not arbitrary-input reliability or a timing benchmark
Only sibling-local frame space is reused; no general register allocator
